profileSignal.note: The description talks about developing novel micro-optics fabrication and alignment methods 'from basic principles to proof of concept and laboratory validation' to create hybrid NIRF-IVUS catheters, which reads as early-stage, foundational technical development rather than applied product engineering.

request.description:
NIRFUS will address the documented need of complementing morphology markers with patho-biological information during intravascular imaging. To enable molecular readings and achieve a breakthrough in interventional cardiology, NIRFUS will implement a new ability in medical micro-optics and address critical obstacles in catheter manufacturing and assembly precision. NIRFUS develops novel concepts and abilities in medical micro-optics by exploring advanced approaches for fabricating and aligning optical components, from basic principles to proof of concept and laboratory validation. 
 These novel methods will enable for the first time the development of clinical-grade near-infrared fluorescence (NIRF) readings added to intravascular ultrasound (IVUS), based on hybrid NIRF-IVUS catheters of unprecedented performance and reliability suitable for human use. NIRFUS will further add complimentary sensing modalities to deliver the most quantitative intravascular NIRF performance ever achieved. The advances in precision engineering, and optical integration, NIRFUS will lead to a new standard of medical micro-optics.
 Likewise, the hybrid NIRF-IVUS catheter will lead to a new standard in interventional imaging and cardiology. NIRFUS may benefit 3 million people who undergo percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) annually by radically improving treatment and clinical outcomes, as well as the efficiency and cost-effectiveness of the global interventional cardiology healthcare, with estimated cost savings of more than € 3.6 billion.

bottomLine: Cisteo MEDICAL already carries €1.1M in EU and French public capital, €569K from the EIC and €506K in state aid over 2025-2026, putting it in the company of FineHeart and CORWAVE, French cardiovascular device makers that drew €302.6M and €323.6M respectively from the same instrument families.
EIC Pathfinder is the right next move: it funds deep-tech work at low technology readiness, matching NIRFUS's work on novel micro-optics fabrication before a working prototype exists.

The French R&D state aid regime via Nouvelle-Aquitaine is a parallel door: it is open, non-dilutive, and administered through Caisse des Dépôts, giving you a national track alongside the EU application.

Skip the ADEME heat-network scheme in this round. Its incentive-effect rule requires the funding application to precede project work, and you have already started work or made firm commitments, so it applies only to future, not current, project costs.
A Pathfinder win brings a grant up to €2.5M for the science-to-technology work plus optional EIC Fund equity of €0.5M-€10M once you reach scale-up, both non-dilutive at the grant stage.

report.positioning: Frame NIRFUS against the EIC's own stated preference for genuine scientific breakthrough at low technology readiness, since Pathfinder scores excellence and high-risk research ambition rather than commercial traction. Your work on novel micro-optics fabrication and alignment methods, still at proof-of-concept and laboratory validation, is exactly the pre-prototype stage the fund rewards, and the counterfactual is clear: clinical-grade NIRF-IVUS catheters cannot be built without solving the precision-manufacturing problem NIRFUS addresses. The European Innovation Council's own 2025 Impact Report frames itself as the investor of choice for deep-tech founders and has mobilised €2.6 billion in additional investment, reinforcing that this is the register to argue in: technological ambition and risk, not market readiness. Keep the pitch on the science-to-technology gap, since your own answers describe the next milestone as working prototypes at clinical-grade reliability, not a commercial deployment story, and the fund does not ask for one.
report.stateOfPlay: The EIC has opened a defence-track call worth €100M as of 2026-06-29, a track distinct from the Pathfinder and Accelerator lines your table draws on, so it signals the EIC is diversifying its calls rather than tightening Pathfinder's own deep-tech criteria. Separately, the EIC is running its European Prize for Humanitarian Innovation, open as of 2026-07-01, which does not touch your route but confirms the EIC is expanding parallel non-dilutive tracks alongside its core Pathfinder and Transition grants. Neither development changes what Pathfinder rewards today, but both point to an EIC that is broadening its instrument mix, worth watching in case a future call structure shifts what a winning Pathfinder application needs to argue.
report.caveats: Figures shown are committed amounts from public registers on each instrument's own reporting basis, coverage varies by country and instrument, and absence from the database is not proof that no funding exists.
